Subject: Moving forward on AWS Private Offer — channel pass-through question

Connor — thanks again for the demo last week. BrightSignal is ready to proceed with an AWS Private Offer but we need to confirm how the channel/reseller (CloudLoop) will be compensated. Two quick asks: 

1) Can Redwood issue the private offer listing with net pricing that allows a 10% pass-through to CloudLoop, or do we need to show a separate commission line on our side?
2) What documentation does Redwood need from CloudLoop (W-9/contract) before the PO is sent to AWS?

I attached our PO input sheet with expected ARR and usage profile. We want to close this before the month-end AWS cycle.

Attachments: [BrightSignal_AWS_PO_Sheet.xlsx (xlsx)]

—Oliver

Subject: Fwd: Moving forward on AWS Private Offer — channel pass-through question

Team — forwarding BrightSignal's ask. TL;DR: external wants a Private Offer that preserves a 10% pass-through to reseller CloudLoop and needs to know what docs we require. BrightSignal expects this to go into AWS before the next listing window (end of May).

Quick checklist I think we need to confirm before I reply to Oliver: 
- Confirm whether we list at net price (including reseller pass-through) or gross price + explicit reseller commission line (affects marketplace revenue recognition).
- Finance: can we support explicit reseller commissions on the PO or should we take a waterfall approach in our accounting? (cc: Lauren)
- Legal: any contract language changes required for reseller pass-through + indemnity? (cc: Irene)
- BizOps: what partner documents do we need pre-listing (W-9, reseller agreement, MSA)? also confirm if CloudLoop needs to be added as an AWS partner alias on the PO. (cc: Karthik)
- Ops: timeline to produce private_offer_template_v2 and sign via DocuSign.

Ben — can you run through an example calc (two scenarios: 10% pass-through from list price vs separate commission line) and attach the calc CSV?
Irene — any quick legal guardrails we should call out?
Lauren — advise on recognition / billing consequences for list vs net.

I'll keep Oliver in the loop but want to align internally first.

Thanks,
Connor

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Moving forward on AWS Private Offer — channel pass-through question

Connor — attached is a quick calc with the two scenarios. Summary: 

Option A — Net-listing (show net price to customer):
- Po list = $1,000,000 ARR
- Reseller pass-through (10%) = $100,000 credited to CloudLoop directly via our invoicing/credit flow
- Redwood GAAP: we record revenue net of reseller pass-through if CloudLoop is acting as an agent (need reseller agreement that defines agency role).

Option B — Gross-listing + commission line:
- Po list = $1,000,000 ARR
- Commission = $100,000 listed as a separate payable to CloudLoop
- Redwood GAAP: revenue recorded gross; commission recognized as cost of sales. This is simpler for AWS PO because it preserves gross list amounts on the private offer.

Ops implications: AWS tends to prefer gross listing with an explicit commission path if the reseller is a distinct invoiced entity. If CloudLoop will be paid by BrightSignal directly, that's different (and simpler).

I attached channel_commission_calc.csv with a 36-month ARR waterfall + example of how credits flow under both approaches. 

Action items from me: 
- Ben: confirm which accounting treatment requires reseller agreement vs agency declaration (next 48h).
- Connor: confirm CloudLoop's preferred collection flow (direct from BrightSignal vs via Redwood).

—Ben
Ben Carter

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightsignal.com>
Cc: partner-ops@cloudloop.io, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Moving forward on AWS Private Offer — channel pass-through question

Oliver — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the PO sheet. We aligned internally and have two viable paths; both are doable but they have different operational impacts. Short answer: we can support a 10% pass-through, but we need to pick the treatment before listing. Recommended next steps (fast path):

1) Pick the gross-listing + commission line approach (Option B) if BrightSignal prefers minimal documentation friction. This preserves gross ARR on the AWS Private Offer and Redwood issues a separate payable to CloudLoop after invoicing.

2) If BrightSignal needs the 10% to be reflected as a net price to the customer (Option A), CloudLoop must sign an agency/reseller addendum (we'll need a reseller agreement and agency declaration). That adds a 5-7 business day lead time.

3) Please confirm how CloudLoop expects to be paid: direct from BrightSignal or via Redwood. If via Redwood, we require CloudLoop's W-9 (US) or equivalent tax form, and a signed reseller addendum. If direct, we only need a written confirmation and partner contact info.

4) Attached is our private offer template (redwood_private_offer_template_v2.pdf) and a DocuSign link to accelerate signing: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-ds/BRI-0458

If you want us to proceed with the fast path (Option B), I'll prepare the private offer, route it for internal finance sign-off, and share the listing window target to AWS. If you prefer Option A, let's start partner onboarding paperwork now. Either way, we can aim to have the PO in the next AWS cycle if we get confirmation by Friday EOD.

Cheers,
Connor
